web_title: 6. 5–10 Year Financial Forensics, Red Flags & Situational Base Rates
book_title: The Forensic Verdict: Stress-Testing the Numbers
question: What do Kody Technolab's P&L, balance sheet, cash flows, and historical robotics base rates tell us about the durability of its business model?

epigraph.quote: A business that grows revenue 97% while operating margins halve and tax spikes to 47% is sending a distress flare about its mix, even if the top line sparkles.
epigraph.author: Forensic Audit Rule

web_blocks.html: Kody Technolab listed on NSE Emerge in September 2023. Its public consolidated record therefore spans FY25, FY26, and H1 FY27 (Sep 2026) [1]. Even in this short window, the four statements show a stark split. Top-line growth is rapid, yet cash and margin quality have weakened sharply.

web_blocks.caption: Consolidated Profit & Loss Summary (FY25, FY26, TTM)
web_blocks.takeaway: Sales accelerated from ₹72 Cr (FY25) to ₹80 Cr (FY26) and ₹111 Cr (TTM), but OPM compressed from 35% to 23% (and 19% in H1 FY27) while Other Income rose to ₹9 Cr TTM.

web_blocks.caption: Consolidated Balance Sheet Summary (Mar 2025 – Sep 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Total assets nearly tripled from ₹112 Cr to ₹298 Cr; Fixed Assets + CWIP jumped from ₹15 Cr to ₹86 Cr, and Borrowings rose from ₹8 Cr (Mar 2026) to ₹27 Cr (Sep 2026).

web_blocks.caption: Consolidated Cash Flow Summary (FY25 – FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: FY26 CFO was only ₹12 Cr against -₹86 Cr Investing CF, producing -₹53 Cr Free Cash Flow funded by +₹113 Cr of Financing CF.

web_blocks.caption: Working Capital & Return Ratios (Mar 2025 – Mar 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Debtor Days worsened from 177 to 192 days and Working Capital Days tripled from 62 to 197 days; FY26 ROCE stood at 17.7% and ROE at 11.4%.

web_blocks.title: Five Forensic Red Flags in H1 FY27 (Sep 2026) & FY26

web_blocks.html: Five warning lights stand out in the latest filings [1]. First, margins collapsed under growth. H1 FY27 sales jumped +97% YoY to ₹62 Cr, yet Operating Profit rose only from ₹8 Cr to ₹12 Cr as OPM% fell from 26% to 19% (down from 35% in FY25) [1]. Second, the effective tax rate spiked to 47% in Sep 2026 [1]. On ₹10 Cr of PBT, tax took nearly half, leaving Net Profit at ₹5 Cr and EPS flat at ₹3.61 [1]. Unabsorbed losses in new subsidiaries likely caused that spike.

Third, receivables and working capital bloated. At 192 debtor days and 197 working capital days, Kody ties up over half a year of sales [1]. Fourth, Other Income props up profits. Other Income hit ₹7 Cr in FY26 (27% of PBT) and ₹9.21 Cr TTM (32% of PBT), masking flat core operating profit (₹25 Cr in FY25 vs ₹26 Cr TTM) [1]. Fifth, FCF is deeply negative and debt is rising. After -₹53 Cr FCF in FY26, borrowings jumped from ₹8 Cr to ₹27 Cr by Sep 2026 [1].

Return ratios also reflect this heavier asset base. FY26 ROCE stood at 17.7%, while ROE was a modest 11.4% [1]. With ₹229 Cr of equity and ₹27 Cr of debt now on the Sep 2026 books, H1 FY27's ₹5 Cr net profit implies an annualized return far below 11% unless H2 margins rebound [1]. Investors should watch H2 FY27 debtor days and cash conversion before assuming a turnaround [1].

web_blocks.company: SoftBank Robotics (Pepper) & Commercial Service-Robot RaaS Pioneers
web_blocks.mechanism: Deployed thousands of interactive humanoid and service robots into retail malls, banks, and hospitality venues on subsidized lease/RaaS models while capitalizing hardware and R&D onto the balance sheet before recurring software/media unit economics proved self-sustaining.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: After producing roughly 27,000 Pepper units, SoftBank halted production in 2020–2021 and cut robotics staff by ~50% as maintenance, depreciation, and customer churn overwhelmed lease revenue.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: High-profile mall and public-venue robot deployments do not guarantee profitable unit economics; if RaaS/pDOOH cash yields lag hardware depreciation and receivable collections, balance-sheet expansion destroys ROE.

web_blocks.title: Pass 1 Price-Blind Verdict: CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL (KPI Health: PASS_WITH_WATCH)
paragraphs: Kody Technolab is not an empty shell. It runs 200+ live robots, holds real UAE contracts (LuLu, Hypermedia, Medigo), and grew H1 FY27 sales +97% YoY. Yet 192 debtor days, -₹53 Cr FCF, 19% OPM, 47% tax, 32% TTM PBT from Other Income, and founder stake sales block a clean pass. Business quality is CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL with KPI health PASS_WITH_WATCH.

book_paragraphs: Now you and I sit down with the full ledger—profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flows, and working-capital ratios—to deliver an honest, price-blind judgment on Kody Technolab's business quality. Forget narratives for five minutes and read what the numbers say when they speak without a press release.

The first thing that jumps off the page is the clash between top-line velocity and bottom-line stagnation. Consolidated sales moved from ₹72 crore in FY25 to ₹80 crore in FY26, and then exploded 97% year-on-year in the first half of FY27 to ₹62 crore, lifting trailing twelve-month sales to ₹111 crore. That is undeniable commercial momentum. Yet look one line down at Operating Profit: ₹25 crore in FY25, ₹24 crore in FY26, and ₹26 crore over the trailing twelve months. Revenue grew by ₹39 crore over that span, and core operating profit grew by just ₹1 crore.

Why did ₹39 crore of incremental revenue yield almost zero incremental operating profit? Because operating margins compressed from 35% in FY25 to 30% in FY26 and down to 19% in the September 2026 half-year. Then, below the operating line in September 2026, depreciation jumped fourfold to ₹4 crore and the effective tax rate spiked to 47%—a classic sign that subsidiary losses are sitting outside the standalone tax shield. The result: on ₹62 crore of H1 FY27 sales, consolidated net profit was only ₹5 crore, producing ₹3.61 in EPS versus ₹3.64 a year earlier.

Now check the balance sheet and cash flow statement. Receivables stretched to 192 days and working capital days tripled to 197 days. Operating cash flow in FY26 was just ₹12 crore against ₹86 crore of investing outflows, leaving Free Cash Flow at minus ₹53 crore. Borrowings jumped from ₹8 crore to ₹27 crore in six months. Meanwhile, Other Income supplied ₹9.21 crore of trailing twelve-month pre-tax profit—nearly one rupee in every three.

History offers a sobering base rate for this exact transition. Between 2014 and 2021, SoftBank Robotics deployed roughly 27,000 Pepper interactive service robots into malls, banks, and retail stores worldwide, betting that recurring software and lease fees would eventually justify heavy upfront hardware capitalization. By 2021, SoftBank halted production and halved its robotics workforce because maintenance, depreciation, and customer churn overwhelmed lease cash flows.

Kody Technolab is not Pepper—its Odigo pDOOH model, UAE LuLu/Hypermedia partnerships, and Medigo manufacturing contract are real commercial footholds, and its +97% revenue surge proves customers are signing up. That is why I do not classify Kody as a fundamental failure. Instead, on a purely price-blind basis, Kody earns a verdict of CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL with KPI health on PASS_WITH_WATCH: an ambitious, fast-growing Physical AI business whose ultimate quality hinges entirely on whether management can collect its 192-day receivables, stabilize margins above 20%, and turn Free Cash Flow positive without endless equity dilution.

Let us summarize the forensic audit checklist you and I will carry forward into the second half of this dossier. On the positive side of the ledger, Kody has scaled consolidated trailing twelve-month revenue to ₹111 crore, maintained positive FY26 ROCE of 17.7% and ROE of 11.4% prior to the H1 FY27 margin squeeze, built real commercial reference accounts in the UAE and India, and avoided collapsing into negative operating cash flow despite rapid growth.

On the skeptical side of the ledger, five concrete warning lights are flashing simultaneously: operating margins fell 1,600 basis points from 35% to 19%; effective tax jumped to 47% in September 2026; Other Income supplies nearly a third of pre-tax profits; debtor days sit at 192 and working capital days at 197; and Free Cash Flow was minus ₹53 crore in FY26 while borrowings tripled to ₹27 crore in H1 FY27.

Notice how clean and objective this price-blind scorecard is. We did not need a single stock quote or valuation multiple to uncover the central tension in Kody Technolab. Whether the company turns out to be a durable Physical AI winner or a capital-trapped hardware experiment will be decided on the collection desk and the depreciation schedule—not in a press release. In Pass 2, when we finally lift the price blindfold, we will test whether the market is paying for 97% revenue growth or already discounting these five forensic realities.

Remember also what the return ratios are telling us. At 17.7% ROCE and 11.4% ROE in FY26—before the September 2026 margin compression and debt jump—Kody was already earning below-elite returns on its freshly raised equity. Unless H2 FY27 and FY28 bring a sharp recovery in operating margins, lower effective tax rates, and faster receivable collections, return on equity will remain under pressure even if top-line growth stays strong.

That is the discipline of a price-blind audit. By locking in our business-quality judgment of CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL and KPI health PASS_WITH_WATCH before ever looking at a share price, we protect ourselves from falling in love with a robotics story whose cash-flow statement is still on probation.

book_callouts.title: The Three KPIs That Decide Kody's Future
book_callouts.text: Before you ever look at a stock chart, write down three operational hurdles for Kody: (1) Debtor days must compress from 192 toward 120 or below; (2) Consolidated OPM must stabilize and expand as Kody Media and UAE fleets mature; (3) Free Cash Flow must turn positive without fresh preferential warrants or rising debt.
